newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bourse higher after wobbly start.
newsitem.headline: French bourse higher after wobbly start.

text.p: French stocks rose on Wednesday after a hesitant start as the bourse absorbed the impact of a widely anticipated quarter-point rise in the U.S. Fed funds rate.
"The dollar's holding up well, and corporate results aren't bad," one trader said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 8.57 points, or 0.33 percent, at 2,632.82 at 1000 GMT after weaving in and out of positive territory in the first hour.
The index had risen 1.74 percent on Tuesday ahead of the interest rate increase.
Shares in electrical equipment supplier Schneider rallied 5.04 percent to 317 francs on better than expected 1996 results.
The company reported net attributable profit surged 61.6 percent to 1.32 billion francs. The market had been expecting a profit of around 1.25 billion francs.

Schneider's results were helped by a sharp drop in net interest expenses to 735 million francs from 1.08 billion, on a big drop in its debt. It raised its net dividend to five francs from four for 1995.

Rumoured merger partners Compagnie de Suez and Lyonnaise extended their recent gains. Suez shares rose 1.2 percent to 284.30 francs, and Lyonnaise's stock was up 0.7 percent at 576 francs. Generale des Eaux confirmed newspaper reports that chairman Jean-Marie Messier does not oppose a merger.
